title: Coffee, brewed, blend of regular and decaffeinated

content.title: About
content.content: Coffee is a beverage made from roasted and ground seeds of the coffee plant. This version is a blend of regular and decaffeinated coffee, offering the full aroma and flavor with reduced caffeine content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Blends of regular and decaf coffee are popular in offices where sustained alertness is needed without strong stimulation.
Decaffeinated coffee is produced either by removing caffeine from green beans or by using naturally low‑caffeine varieties.
The aromatic profile of the blend can be more balanced, as decaf softens the bitterness of regular coffee.
Coffee is the second most traded commodity in the world after oil.
There are over 100 species of coffee plants, but commercially only Arabica and Robusta are widely cultivated.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Coffee is rich in polyphenols that help combat free radicals and may lower the risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: Cognitive support
items.content: Moderate coffee consumption is linked to improved attention, memory, and reaction time.

items.title: Reduced risk of type 2 diabetes
items.content: Studies suggest regular coffee drinking can decrease the likelihood of developing diabetes.

items.title: Liver protection
items.content: Coffee consumption is associated with a lower risk of cirrhosis and some liver cancers.

items.title: Metabolism boost
items.content: Caffeine speeds up metabolism, which can aid weight management.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat even with small amounts of caffeine.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Coffee can irritate the stomach in people with gastritis or acid reflux.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Caffeine may amplify the effects of certain stimulants and diminish the efficacy of some sedatives.

items.title: Pregnancy
items.content: Pregnant women are advised to limit caffeine intake to 200 mg per day.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use 1‑2 teaspoons of ground coffee per 180‑200 ml of hot water (90‑95 °C) and steep for 3‑5 minutes. The blend works well for drip, French press, or espresso machines. Add milk, cream, or plant‑based alternatives if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ground coffee in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Keep it away from air, moisture, and light to preserve aroma and flavor. Shelf life is about 3‑6 months after opening.
